title: Move the object away
hook: Change object distance and predict magnification magnitude.

doesNotKnow: magnification magnitude = image distance / object distance

misconception: magnification magnitude doubles when object distance doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply magnification magnitude = image distance / object distance to compare magnification magnitude when object distance changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With thin-lens configurations with fixed image distance and refocusing lenses of different focal lengths, magnification magnitude = image distance / object distance. When object distance doubles, magnification magnitude becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model magnification magnitude = image distance / object distance; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider thin-lens configurations with fixed image distance and refocusing lenses of different focal lengths, with a nonzero initial result. If object distance triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on magnification magnitude?
recall.why: Apply magnification magnitude = image distance / object distance under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
